items.note: Two poetry-writing experiments compare writing alone with editing an AI-generated poem (Study 1) and co-creating with AI (Study 2), with poem creativity as the outcome; the abstract gives neither N nor the assignment method.

Participants are primed with word lists said to come from a human or from ChatGPT, at three creativity levels, and then complete the Divergent Association Task; the AI manipulation is a source label on priming stimuli rather than real AI assistance, so the next stage should check whether it fits the scope.

Between-subjects brainstorming experiment (n = 75) compares solitary humans with human-GPT-3.5 dyads on fluency, flexibility, novelty, and value of ideas; the abstract does not state random assignment.

Conceptual framework (taxonomy of seven metacognitive capacities) explaining why AI raises individual creativity but lowers collective diversity; no data; the arXiv version 2606.05532 is the same work.

Between-subjects experiment (N = 244) compares four human-AI interaction designs for a persona-creation task on rated creativity, originality, and between-persona similarity; all arms use AI (AI configuration versus AI configuration), and the abstract does not state random assignment.

Engineering students solve three TRIZ problems with and without LLM support, with design quality plus workload and perceived usefulness as outcomes; the abstract gives neither N nor the assignment method.
Meta-analysis of 56 experimental studies (9,643 participants in total) on AI-supported instruction and students' creative thinking (SMD = 0.54); it covers AI broadly, not only generative AI.

Co-located groups do creative marketing tasks with generative AI or a web search engine, and external raters score the results in a second study; the abstract gives neither N nor the assignment method, and the unit of analysis is the group (abstract from Semantic Scholar).

System paper with a within-subjects study (N = 32) comparing a baseline with low- and high-semantic-similarity GenAI visual inspirations for drawing; it reports higher divergent thinking than baseline, but the abstract does not say whether that was scored on drawings, whether the baseline uses AI, or whether order was counterbalanced; below 50 participants.

Observational analysis of NSF and NIH proposals from two R1 universities and all public awards, finding that higher LLM involvement goes with lower semantic distinctiveness of proposals; same work as arXiv 2601.15485.
